diagnostics.interpretation: Exploratory projection of text representations; two-dimensional distances are lossy and are not evidence of biological relationships. Neighbors use original-space cosine similarity.

input_policy.duplicate_blocks: Deduplicate canonical identity/label/description text, retaining every native record reference
input_policy.gap_fields: Nonempty fields in terms.iter_item_texts order; original text retained
input_policy.missing_descriptions: Retain native label and identifier; no synthetic definition or curation-note fallback
input_policy.record_order: Canonical identity, native label, then native description
input_policy.record_scope: Every native owner of an accepted matched term; no recursive recognition
input_policy.text_budget: Complete text; encoder must chunk rather than silently truncate

encoding_policy.chunks: Non-overlapping consecutive content-token spans of at most 480 tokens
encoding_policy.document_pooling: Content-token-count-weighted mean of chunk vectors, then L2 normalization
encoding_policy.precision: float32 inference and retained vectors; float64 weighted accumulation
encoding_policy.special_tokens: One BERT CLS token before and SEP token after every chunk
encoding_policy.tokenization: Pinned BERT tokenizer; entire input; no special tokens or truncation

runtime.reproducibility: Pinned inputs, model and runtime; retained vectors and coordinates are authoritative. Cross-device or cross-version floating-point identity is not asserted.

records.description: A heterodimeric transcription factor complex composed of proteins from the c-Fos, c-Jun, activating transcription factor (ATF) or JDP families. The subunits contain a basic leucine zipper (bZIP) domain that is essential for dimerization and DNA binding. Jun-Fos heterodimers bind preferentially to a heptamer consensus sequence (TPA responsive element (TRE)), whereas Jun-ATF dimers bind the cyclic AMP responsive element (CRE) to regulate transcription of target genes.
records.label: transcription factor AP-1 complex

records.description: A membrane-bounded intracellular vesicle formed by invagination of the plasma membrane around an extracellular substance. Endocytic vesicles fuse with early endosomes to deliver the cargo for further sorting.
records.label: endocytic vesicle

records.description: A pigment-bearing structure that is derived from the cytoplasmic membrane, sometimes consisting of simple invaginations and sometimes a complete vesicle. This component is found in certain photosynthetic bacteria and cyanobacteria.
records.label: plasma membrane-derived chromatophore

records.description: The regulated release of mucus by the mucosa. Mucus is a viscous slimy secretion consisting of mucins and various inorganic salts dissolved in water, with suspended epithelial cells and leukocytes. The mucosa, or mucous membrane, is the membrane covered with epithelium that lines the tubular organs of the body. Mucins are carbohydrate-rich glycoproteins that have a lubricating and protective function.
records.label: mucus secretion

records.description: Two separate septin rings that are formed from the septin collar at the time of cytokinesis in cells that divide by budding. These two rings are thought to delineate a special compartment in which factors involved in cytokinesis are concentrated.
records.label: cellular bud neck split septin rings

records.description: A region of the ventral disc of Giardia species (trophozoite stage) where two portions of the same array of microtubules overlap (the microtubule array makes a complete circle and overlaps on itself).
records.label: ventral disc overlap zone

records.description: A homodimeric mismatch repair complex involved in binding to and correcting insertion/deletion mutations.
records.label: MutS complex

records.description: A Lamassu system in which an organism possesses a locus encoding the LmuA effector and SMC-like LmuB sensor but no LmuC component.
records.label: Lamassu type I system

definition_sources: NCBIfam PGAP (composed from product and EC/GO annotations)
records.description: CDK-activating kinase assembly factor MAT1 — a functionally conserved protein family grouped by the NCBIfam full-length profile-HMM TIGR00570 (equivalog); associated with nucleotide-excision repair complex, cyclin-dependent protein serine/threonine kinase activity, transcription factor TFIIH holo complex, nucleotide-excision repair.
records.label: CDK-activating kinase assembly factor MAT1

records.description: The pairwise union of individuals for the purpose of sexual reproduction, ultimately resulting in the formation of zygotes.
records.label: mating

records.description: A complex that loads the DNA polymerase processivity factor proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) onto DNA, thereby permitting processive DNA synthesis catalyzed by DNA polymerase. In eukaryotes the complex consists of five polypeptides.
records.label: DNA replication factor C complex

records.description: A protein complex that contains the GINS complex, Cdc45p, and the heterohexameric MCM complex, and that is involved in unwinding DNA during replication.
records.label: CMG complex

records.description: The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding a cilium.
records.label: ciliary membrane

records.description: The peptidoglycan layer of the Gram-negative cell envelope. In Gram-negative cells the peptidoglycan is relatively thin (1-2nm) and is linked to the outer membrane by lipoproteins. In Gram-negative cells the peptidoglycan is too thin to retain the primary stain in the Gram staining procedure and therefore cells appear red after Gram stain.
records.label: Gram-negative-bacterium-type cell wall

records.description: A cell arrangement in which dividing cocci form irregular three-dimensional grape-like clusters because division planes occur in multiple, non-orthogonal orientations and daughter cells remain attached.
records.label: staphylococcus arrangement

records.description: The region where the mating projection meets the bulk of the cell, in unicellular fungi exposed to mating pheromone.
records.label: mating projection base

records.description: The lipid bilayer surrounding the vacuole and separating its contents from the cytoplasm of the cell.
records.label: vacuolar membrane

records.description: The DNA polymerase III core complex consists of the alpha,epsilon and theta subunits and is carries out the polymerase and the 3'-5' exonuclease proofreading activities.
records.label: DNA polymerase III, core complex

records.description: The double lipid bilayer enclosing the cyanelle and separating its contents from the rest of the cytoplasm; includes the intermembrane space.
records.label: cyanelle envelope

records.description: A metabolism in which an organism reduces nitrate, whether for energy conservation or for assimilation into biomass.
records.label: nitrate reduction

records.description: An incomplete microtubule containing 10 protofilaments that fuses with a complete microtubule called A tubule (containing 13 protofilaments) to form an axonemal outer doublet.
records.label: B axonemal microtubule

records.description: A phenotype that is describing how an organism obtains carbon and energy for growth and metabolism.
records.label: trophic type

records.description: tRNA-guanine transglycosylase DpdA — a functionally conserved protein family grouped by the NCBIfam full-length profile-HMM NF041059 (equivalog); associated with tRNA modification, glycosyltransferase activity.
records.label: tRNA-guanine transglycosylase DpdA

records.description: A multi-subunit complex embedded in the mitochondrial inner membrane that mediates the inner membrane insertion of multi-transmembrane spanning proteins that contain internal targeting elements. In yeast cells, TIM22 is a 300-kDa complex, consisting of four membrane integral subunits, Tim22, Tim54, Tim18 and Sdh3, and a peripheral chaperone complex consisting of the small TIM proteins, Tim9-Tim10-Tim12.
records.label: TIM22 mitochondrial import inner membrane insertion complex

records.description: A phenotype that is relating to an organism's ability to form dormant, stress-resistant endospores.
records.label: sporulation

records.description: A pointed projection of the skin on the head of various animals, consisting of a covering of horn (keratin and other proteins) surrounding a core of living bone.
records.label: horn

records.description: A protein complex that inhibits unwinding of DNA at the origin of replication and assembly of the pre-primosome. In E. coli, this complex is composed of DnaA and of the ribosomal protein L2.
records.label: DnaA-L2 complex

definition_sources: InterPro:IPR045238 abstract (PANTHER PTHR15371 is a member signature)
records.description: This entry includes mitochondrial import inner membrane translocase subunit Tim23 and chloroplastic outer envelope pore protein 16-1/2 (OEP161/162). In plants OEP161/162 are distantly related to the translocase of the inner mitochondrial membrane Tim17. OEP161/162 are amino acid-selective channel proteins and translocation pores for NADPH:protochlorophyllide oxidoreductase A (PORA). The TIM23 complex forms a dynamic multisubunit machinery that recognises preproteins and can transport them into the inner membrane or into the matrix. It is composed of three subunits, Tim50, Tim23, and Tim17, that expose the domains to the intermembrane space. This entry includes the mitochondrial import inner membrane translocase subunit Tim23, consisting of an N-terminal intermembrane space domain that interacts with Tim50, and a C-terminal membrane-embedded domain that, together with Tim17, forms a protein-conducting channel across the inner membrane. Tim50 helps keeping the Tim23 channel in a closed state in the absence of presequence proteins, regulating the gating through the TIM channel.
records.label: TIM23

records.description: The outermost lipid bilayer surrounding complex plastids in organisms that acquired their plastids through secondary endosymbiosis. This membrane is derived from the host cell's endomembrane system and is continuous with the rough endoplasmic reticulum and the outer nuclear envelope. In some species, the cytoplasmic face may be studded with ribosomes.
records.label: epiplastidial membrane

records.description: SCOPe dm-level node 'Structural proteins' (sccs i.6.1.1).
records.label: Structural proteins

records.description: SCOPe cl-level node 'Peptides' (sccs j).
records.label: Peptides

records.description: Spt5 C-terminal nonapeptide repeat binding Spt4. Pfam repeat family CTD (Pfam:PF12815).
records.label: Spt5 C-terminal nonapeptide repeat binding Spt4

records.description: MZA anti-phage system associated ATPase MzaB — a functionally conserved protein family grouped by the NCBIfam full-length profile-HMM NF041932 (equivalog); associated with defense response to virus. Members occur in Pseudomonadota.
records.label: MZA anti-phage system associated ATPase MzaB

records.description: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial eukaryote internalizes the intact axoneme of its own cilium or flagellum into its cell body.
records.label: eukaryotic flagellar axoneme internalization

records.description: Responsible for the transport of xenobiotics, such as drugs, out of the cell, in particular from the periplasm. Single-component efflux transporters remove toxic compounds from the cytoplasm to the periplasmic space where tolC-dependent transporters expel them from the cell. Capable of recognizing a wide range of dissimilar lipophilic and amphiphilic substrates that may differ in structure, size or electrical charge. These include beta-lactams, quinolones, tetracyclines, chloramphenicol and steroid hormones. Substrate specificity is conferred by a pair of large periplasmic loops containing more than 300 amino acid residues each. Member of the Resistance-Nodulation-Division (RND) family of efflux pumps. A curated stable macromolecular complex (Complex Portal) with 3 subunits.
records.label: AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux transport complex

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses an Eleos locus represented by LeoA, LeoB, LeoBC, and LeoC profiles that can protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection.
records.label: Eleos system

records.description: A protein complex containing homohexameric DNA helicase DnaB, and the DNA helicase loader DnaC. The helicase loader DnaC delivers DnaB to the chromosomal origin (oriC).
records.label: DnaB-DnaC complex

records.description: A spherical, membrane-bounded organelle found in some anaerobic protozoa, which participates in ATP and molecular hydrogen formation.
records.label: hydrogenosome

records.description: A small mass of living substance capable of developing into an organism or one of its parts.
records.label: germ

records.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of RNA, ribonucleic acid, one of the two main type of nucleic acid, consisting of a long, unbranched macromolecule formed from ribonucleotides joined in 3',5'-phosphodiester linkage. Includes polymerization of ribonucleotide monomers. Refers not only to transcription but also to e.g. viral RNA replication.
records.label: RNA biosynthetic process

records.description: The core TFIIH complex when it is part of the nucleotide-excision repair factor 3 (NEF3).
records.label: core TFIIH complex portion of NEF3 complex

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a Druantia locus encoding a conserved DruE-family core and subtype-specific partner proteins.
records.label: Druantia system

records.description: An abortive infection system in which an organism possesses a PD-T4-10 locus represented by DefenseFinder as a two-profile model, PD-T4-10__PD-T4-10_A and PD-T4-10__PD-T4-10_B, and experimentally linked to T2, T4, T6, T5, and SECphi27 protection when expressed in E. coli.
records.label: PD-T4-10 system

records.description: The region of the prospore membrane to which the spindle pole body (SPB) is anchored; the prospore membrane extends from the SPB attachment site to surround the spore nucleus.
records.label: prospore membrane spindle pole body attachment site

records.description: A complex composed of two proteins, prohibitin 1 and prohibitin 2 (PHB1/PHB-1 and PHB2/PHB-2) that is highly conserved amongst eukaryotes and associated with the inner mitochondrial membrane. The mitochondrial prohibitin complex is a macromolecular supercomplex composed of repeating heterodimeric subunits of PHB1 and PHB2. The mitochondrial prohibitin complex plays a role in a number of biological processes, including mitochondrial biogenesis and function, development, replicative senescence, and cell death.
records.label: mitochondrial prohibitin complex

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a TIR-I locus, represented in the pinned DefenseFinder HMM inventory by TIR-I__TIR-I_A and TIR-I__TIR-I_B custom profiles, that can inhibit bacteriophage plaquing.
records.label: TIR-I system

records.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of ATP, adenosine 5'-triphosphate, a universally important coenzyme and enzyme regulator.
records.label: ATP biosynthetic process

records.description: The lipid bilayer surrounding a vesicle transporting substances between the trans-Golgi network and other parts of the cell.
records.label: trans-Golgi network transport vesicle membrane

records.description: SCOPe cl-level node 'Artifacts' (sccs l).
records.label: Artifacts

records.description: Key role in mRNA degradation and RNA processing. RNA binds to RnaE, RhlB helicase is necessary to unwind the RNA secondary structures and, once unwound, the 3'-5' decay of the transcripts is ensued by phosphate-dependent PNPase. RNase E bound-enolase may connect cellular metabolic status with post-transcriptional gene regulation and link RNA degradation to glycolytic processes. A dynamic set of minor components of this complex may regulate its function and compartmentalization. A curated stable macromolecular complex (Complex Portal) with 4 subunits.
records.label: RNA degradosome

records.description: An elongated depression or channel along the surface of a protein structure.
records.label: groove

records.description: A septin collar in pathogenic fungi involved in the constriction of hyphae at the plant plasmodesma enabling penetration of an adjacent cell.
records.label: hyphae septin collar

records.description: A complex glycopeptide from Streptomyces orientalis. It inhibits a specific step in the synthesis of the peptidoglycan layer in the Gram-positive bacteria Staphylococcus aureus and Clostridium difficile.
records.label: vancomycin

records.description: A long and narrow elevation with steep sides.
records.label: ridge

records.description: The plastid organelle found in apicomplexans.
records.label: apicoplast

records.description: The layer in a bacterial endospore that lies under the exosporium, and is impermeable to many toxic molecules. The coat may also contain enzymes that are involved in endospore germination.
records.label: endospore coat

records.description: A vacuole that has both lytic and storage functions. The fungal vacuole is a large, membrane-bounded organelle that functions as a reservoir for the storage of small molecules (including polyphosphate, amino acids, several divalent cations (e.g. calcium), other ions, and other small molecules) as well as being the primary compartment for degradation. It is an acidic compartment, containing an ensemble of acid hydrolases. At least in S. cerevisiae, there are indications that the morphology of the vacuole is variable and correlated with the cell cycle, with logarithmically growing cells having a multilobed, reticulated vacuole, while stationary phase cells contain a single large structure.
records.label: fungal-type vacuole

records.description: The portion of the central rod of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body that is proximal to the cell membrane; the proximal rod connects the distal rod to the flagellar motor.
records.label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, proximal rod

records.description: A quality that differentiates specific instances of a species from other instances of the same species.
records.label: phenotype

records.description: Catalysis of the reaction: L-lysine + H+ = cadaverine + CO2.
records.label: lysine decarboxylase activity

records.description: A conserved heterotrimeric complex that binds nonspecifically to single-stranded DNA and is required for multiple processes in eukaryotic DNA metabolism, including DNA replication, DNA repair, and recombination. In all eukaryotic organisms examined the complex is composed of subunits of approximately 70, 30, and 14 kDa.
records.label: DNA replication factor A complex

records.description: A filamentous outgrowth; especially: an epidermal hair structure on a plant.
records.label: trichome

records.description: A heterooligomeric protein complex that spans the bacterial periplasm and enables the secretion of adhesin proteins in Gram-negative bacteria. In Citrobacter rodentium, Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli, the TAM complex consists of an Omp85-family protein, TamA, in the outer membrane and TamB in the inner membrane.
records.label: TAM protein secretion complex

records.description: A protein complex that contains a histone deacetylase and is part of the chromatin remodeling machinery. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae this complex contains the Rpd3p, Sin3p, Ume1p, Pho23p, Sap30p, Sds3p, Cti6p, Rxt2p, Rxt3p, Dep1p, Ume6p, Ash1p, Dot6p, Snt1, Sif2p, Set3p, Hos2p, Tos4p and Tod6p proteins.
records.label: Rpd3L-Expanded complex

definition_sources: NCBIfam PGAP (composed from product and EC/GO annotations)
records.description: archaellum stator protein ArlF — a functionally conserved protein family grouped by the NCBIfam full-length profile-HMM NF052590 (equivalog); associated with archaeal-type flagellum, archaeal-type flagellum-dependent cell motility. Members occur in Methanobacteriota.
records.label: archaellum stator protein ArlF

records.description: A nitrogen respiration in which nitrate is the terminal electron acceptor, reduced to nitrite or further reduced products.
records.label: nitrate respiration

records.description: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of a toxic substance. These may include transport of the toxic substance away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of the toxic substance.
records.label: detoxification

records.description: A meroterpenoid resulting from the formal condensation of the hydroxy group of fumagillol with the carboxylic acid group of (all-E)-deca-2,4,6,8-tetraenedioic acid. Originally isolated from the fungus Aspergillus fumigatus, it is used for the control of Nosema infection in honey bees.
records.label: fumagillin

records.description: A bacteroid-containing symbiosome in which the bacterial component is a genetically highly reduced cyanobacterium that is photosynthetically active
records.label: organellar chromatophore

records.description: Inner arm structure present on the outer doublet microtubules of ciliary and flagellar axonemes. The structure of inner dynein arms is complex and may vary within the axoneme. Inner dynein arms are heteromeric, comprising 8 different heavy chains and various subunits. Inner and outer dynein arms have different functions in the generation of microtubule-based motility.
records.label: inner dynein arm

records.description: An anaerobic respiration in which an organism uses chlorate as the terminal electron acceptor and reduces it to chloride for energy conservation.
records.label: chlorate respiration

records.description: Nuclear bodies frequently found near or associated with Cajal bodies (also called coiled bodies or CBs). Gemini of coiled bodies, or 'gems', are similar in size and shape to CBs, and often indistinguishable under the microscope. Unlike CBs, gems do not contain small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs); they contain a protein called survivor of motor neurons (SMN) whose function relates to snRNP biogenesis. Gems are believed to assist CBs in snRNP biogenesis, and to play a role in the etiology of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).
records.label: Gemini of Cajal bodies

records.description: A motile phenotype in which the speed of active propulsion is modulated according to orientation relative to gravity.
records.label: gravikinesis

records.description: A heterooligomeric septin complex that acts during meiotic cell division.
records.label: meiotic septin complex

records.description: The lipid membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cytoplasm from the external environment and houses proteins for selective transport, signaling, and envelope biogenesis.
records.label: plasma membrane

records.description: The process of introducing a phosphate group on to a protein.
records.label: protein phosphorylation

records.description: Pertaining or relating to protozoa of the order Kinetoplastida.
records.label: kinetoplastid

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses an Esos locus represented by a VCA0450 profile that can protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection.
records.label: Esos system

records.description: The volume enclosed by a thylakoid membrane.
records.label: thylakoid lumen

records.description: Stable, specialized structure for the ingestion of food by the cell into phagosomes.
records.label: cytostome

records.description: A ribonuclease P complex located in the cyanelle, where it catalyzes the 5' endonucleolytic cleavage of precursor tRNAs to yield mature tRNAs. The best characterized cyanelle ribonuclease P complex, from the alga Cyanophora paradoxa, contains a single RNA molecule that is necessary but not sufficient for catalysis, and several protein molecules.
records.label: cyanelle ribonuclease P complex

records.description: A C-type aurachin that is quinolin-4-one which is substituted by a hydroxy group at positions 1, a methyl group at position 2, and a triprenyl group at position 3.
records.label: aurachin C

records.description: A large ribonucleoprotein complex considered to be the earliest preribosomal complex. In S. cerevisiae, it has a size of 90S and consists of the 35S pre-rRNA, early-associating ribosomal proteins most of which are part of the small ribosomal subunit, the U3 snoRNA and associated proteins.
records.label: 90S preribosome

records.description: An extracellular hollow tubular archaeal cell projection, characterized in Pyrodictium species, that extends from the cell envelope as a proteinaceous filament and forms networks between cells.
records.label: archaeal cannula

records.description: One of several protein complexes involved in nucleotide-excision repair; possesses endodeoxynuclease and DNA helicase activities. In S. cerevisiae, it is composed of Rad2p and the core TFIIH-Ssl2p complex (core TFIIH is composed of Rad3p, Tfb1p, Tfb2p, Ssl1p, Tfb4p and Tfb5p. Note that Ssl2p is also called Rad25p).
records.label: nucleotide-excision repair factor 3 complex

records.description: An autophagy phenotype in which a microbial cell degrades parts of its nucleus or an entire nucleus by delivering nuclear material to lysosomal or vacuolar compartments.
records.label: nucleophagy

records.description: Enzymatic activity — hydrazine synthase (EC 1.7.2.7). Catalysed reaction: hydrazine + 3 Fe(III)-[cytochrome c] + H2O = nitric oxide + 3 Fe(II)- [cytochrome c] + NH4(+) + 2 H(+).
records.label: hydrazine synthase

records.description: A microtubule located such that it threads through the conoid and projects through the polar ring.
records.label: intraconoid microtubule

records.description: A morphological phenotype in which a fungus forms linear multihyphal cords by aggregation behind an extending margin of diffuse hyphae.
records.label: fungal mycelial cord formation

records.description: That part of the plasma membrane found in the ciliary pocket (also called flagellar pocket).
records.label: ciliary pocket membrane

records.description: The membrane-associated protein machine that builds the peptidoglycan division septum in FtsZ-dependent bacterial cytokinesis. Membrane-tethered FtsZ filaments organize the division site and help distribute septal synthases; movement during active synthesis is not universally driven by FtsZ treadmilling.
records.label: divisome complex

records.description: The element Y, distinct from its trivalent ion, experimental chloride salt, host minerals and rare-earth commodity mixtures. The dated US designation concerns the named yttrium mineral commodity; it does not establish criticality of every Y-bearing substance. Laboratory evidence concerns yttrium associated with washed algal biomass, without establishing intracellular transport, isolated-product recovery or industrial deployment.
records.label: Yttrium

records.description: An arrangement of closely apposed microtubules running parallel to each other.
records.label: microtubule bundle

records.description: A membrane-bounded organelle found in a microsporidian spore that swells with water and exerts pressure to rupture the polar cap and evert the polar tube.
records.label: polaroplast

records.description: A structure lying external to one or more cells, which provides structural support, biochemical or biomechanical cues for cells or tissues.
records.label: extracellular matrix

records.description: The space enclosed by the double membrane of a cyanelle.
records.label: cyanelle stroma

records.description: A fermentation in which solventogenic bacteria convert organic carbon sources to organic acids and then reassimilate those acids to produce acetone, butanol, and ethanol solvents.
records.label: acetone-butanol-ethanol fermentation

records.description: A chromosome that encodes the nuclear genome and is found in the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell during the cell cycle phases when the nucleus is intact.
records.label: nuclear chromosome

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses an Oshun locus that can protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection.
records.label: Oshun system

records.description: A nitrification metabolism in which a single organism oxidizes ammonia via nitrite to nitrate.
records.label: complete ammonia oxidation

records.description: The volume enclosed by the membrane of a late endosome.
records.label: late endosome lumen

records.description: An intracellular non-membrane-bounded organelle; a hollow structure made of protein, which usually has the form of a cylindrical tube closed by conical end caps. By regulating their relative gas vesicle content, aquatic microbes are able to perform vertical migrations.
records.label: gas vesicle

records.description: A cyclic carotene obtained by dimerisation of all-trans-retinol. A strongly-coloured red-orange pigment abundant in plants and fruit and the most active and important provitamin A carotenoid.
records.label: β-carotene

records.description: A eukaryotically conserved histone deacetylase complex which deacetylates histones across gene coding regions. Composed of a catalytic histone deacetylase subunit, a chromodomain protein, a SIN3 family co-repressor, and a WD repeat protein (Clr6p, Alp13p, Pst2p, and Prw1p respectively in Schizosaccharomyces; Rpd3p, Sin3p, Ume1p, Rco1p and Eaf3 in Saccharomyces; homologs thereof in other species).
records.label: Rpd3S complex

records.description: The process preceding formation of the peptide bond between the first two amino acids of a protein. This includes the formation of a complex of the ribosome, mRNA or circRNA, and an initiation complex that contains the first aminoacyl-tRNA.
records.label: translational initiation

records.description: A system which has the disposition to environ one or more material entities.
records.label: environmental system

records.description: Conserved heterotrimeric complex of PCNA-like proteins that is loaded onto DNA at sites of DNA damage.
records.label: checkpoint clamp complex

records.description: A complex of approximately 20 proteins, most of which are located in the cytoplasmic membrane that carries out protein secretion in the bacterial type III secretion system; type III secretion also requires a cytoplasmic, probably membrane-associated ATPase.
records.label: type III protein secretion system complex

records.description: A biomineralization phenotype in which a diatom forms the siliceous valve and girdle-band elements of its cell wall (frustule).
records.label: diatom frustule production

records.description: A layer surrounding a bacterial endospore found inside the outer endospore membrane, but outside the membrane surrounding the endospore core. It consists of peptidoglycan of a different chemical nature than that found in vegetative cell walls which results in less cross-linking of peptidoglycan.
records.label: endospore cortex

records.description: One of three laminate structures that form the mitotic spindle pole body; the central plaque is embedded in the nuclear envelope.
records.label: central plaque of mitotic spindle pole body

records.description: A complex that functions in anterograde transport at the Golgi and also regulates autophagy. In yeast it includes at least the following subunits: Bet3 (as homodimer), Bet5, Trs20, Trs23, Trs31, Trs33, Trs85. TRAPPIII may include further, as yet undescribed, proteins.
records.label: TRAPPIII protein complex

records.description: The series of molecular signals that forms a pathway of communication from the mitochondria to the nucleus and initiates cellular changes in response to changes in mitochondrial function.
records.label: mitochondria-nucleus signaling pathway

records.description: A biological process that maintain life in an organism.
records.label: metabolism

records.description: A discrete intracellular part formed of aggregated molecules such as proteins or other biopolymers.
records.label: inclusion body

records.description: The increase in size or mass of an anatomical structure that contributes to the structure attaining its shape.
records.label: developmental growth involved in morphogenesis

records.description: A nucleoplasmic speckle distributed in the interchromatin space of cells in close proximity to chromatin. Omega speckles are distinct from interchromatin granules and contain heterogeneous nuclear RNA-binding proteins (hnRNPs).
records.label: omega speckle

records.description: A polyketide antibiotic that is isolated from Actinosynnema pretiosum and also exhibits antitumour activity.
records.label: ansamitocin P3

records.description: The lipid bilayer surrounding a peroxisome.
records.label: peroxisomal membrane

records.description: A type of autophagy where cytosolic components are ingested by late endosomes, lysosomes or yeast-type lytic vacuoles by direct invagination of the compartment membrane without prior sequestration into an autophagosome. The engulfing membranes fuse, resulting in the lysosomal delivery of the cargo wrapped in a single membrane derived from the invaginated lysosomal membrane.
records.label: microautophagy

records.description: A class of nuclear body measuring 20-25 nm in diameter and distributed throughout the interchromatin space, linked together by thin fibrils. They are believed to be storage centers for various snRNAs, snRNPs, serine/arginine-rich proteins and RNA polymerase II. A typical mammalian cell contains 25-50 clusters of interchromatin granules. Interchromatin granule clusters do not contain the heterogeneous nuclear RNA-binding proteins (hnRNPs).
records.label: interchromatin granule

records.description: Growth of a plant structure from the time of its initiation by an apical meristem until its expansion is completed.
records.label: primary growth

records.description: SCOPe dm-level node 'Nsp1' (sccs d.346.1.1).
records.label: Nsp1

records.description: A speleothem which consists of a macroscopic acicular mineral crystal, most commonly aragonite, precipitated subaerially from an evaporating capillary or seepage film on a cave surface or coralloid nodule.
records.label: cave spicule

records.description: The volume enclosed by a cytoplasmic vesicle.
records.label: cytoplasmic vesicle lumen

records.description: TraB is a homolog of VirB10 which forms part of core complex in Type IV secretion system (T4SS). This family contains TraB (VirB10 homolog) and a component of the type IV secretion system (T4SS), and similar proteins. T4S system is employed by pathogenic bacteria to export virulence DNAs and/or proteins directly from the bacterial cytoplasm into the host cell. It forms a large multiprotein complex consisting of 12 proteins termed VirB1-11 and VirD4. VirB10, interacts with VirB7 and VirB9, forming the membrane-spanning 'core complex' (CC), around which all other components assemble. The CC is inserted in both the outer and inner membranes, playing a fundamental role as a scaffold for the rest of the T4SS components and actively participating in T4S substrate transfer through the bacterial envelope via conformational changes regulating channel opening and closing. TraB is localized similarly to related proteins in other systems, but unlike in other systems, Neisseria gonorrhoeae TraB does not require the presence of other T4SS components for proper localization. It has been shown to be expressed with TraK (VirB9 homolog) at low levels in wild-type cells, suggesting that gonococcal T4SS may be present in single copy per cell and the small amounts of these proteins are sufficient for DNA secretion

records.description: A monohydroxyquinoline that is 4-hydroxyquinoline bearing an additional heptyl substituent at position 2.
records.label: 2-heptyl-4-hydroxyquinoline

records.description: A tight ring-shaped structure that forms in the division plane within hyphae of filamentous fungi at sites where a septum will form; composed of septins as well as septin-associated proteins.
records.label: hyphal septin ring

records.description: An exocytotic phenotype in which a microbial cell releases trichocyst contents to the exterior through fusion of a trichocyst membrane with the plasma membrane.
records.label: trichocyst discharge

records.description: A systematic error introduced into sampling or testing by selecting or encouraging one outcome or answer over others.
records.label: Bias

records.description: Interaction between molecules within the same physical complex. Often identified under conditions which suggest that the molecules are in close proximity but not necessarily in direct contact with each other.
records.label: physical association

records.description: A trophic type in which an organism obtains carbon from organic compounds rather than from carbon dioxide.
records.label: heterotrophic

records.description: The evagination of a membrane, resulting in formation of a vesicle.
records.label: vesicle budding from membrane

records.description: Any protein complex that is part of the plasma membrane.
records.label: plasma membrane protein complex

records.description: A spliceosomal complex that is formed by the recruitment of the preassembled U4atac/U6atac.U5 tri-snRNP to the U12-type prespliceosome. Although all 5 snRNPs are present, the precatalytic spliceosome is catalytically inactive. The precatalytic spliceosome includes many proteins in addition to those found in the U11, U12 and U4atac/U6atac.U5 snRNPs.
records.label: U12-type precatalytic spliceosome

records.description: A protein complex capable of FMN reductase activity. Reduces FMN to FMNH2 in a NAD(P)H-dependent manner. In E.coli, consists of a SsuE dimer.
records.label: FMN reductase complex

records.description: A ribonucleoprotein complex that contains the extensively base paired small nuclear RNAs U4atac and U6atac, a heptameric ring of Sm proteins associated with U4atac, the Lsm2-8 heptameric ring complex associated with U6atac, as well as several proteins that are unique to the U4atac snRNP or U6atac snRNPs, some of which remain associated with the U4atac/U6atac snRNA both while the U4atac snRNP is free or assembled into a series of spliceosomal complexes.
records.label: U4atac/U6atac snRNP

records.description: A membrane-bounded vesicle found predominantly in Plasmodium female gametocytes, that becomes progressively more abundant as the gametocyte reaches full maturity. These vesicles lie beneath the subpellicular membrane of the gametocyte, and the release of their contents into the parasitophorous vacuole has been postulated to aid in the escape of gametocytes from the erythrocyte after ingestion by the mosquito.
records.label: osmiophilic body

records.description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of prolonged deprivation of water that restores that organism to a normal (non-stressed) condition.
records.label: drought recovery

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a VP1839-family locus represented by the DefenseFinder VP1839__VP1839 custom HMM profile and experimentally linked to reduced bacteriophage plaquing when the cloned Vibrio parahaemolyticus RIMD 2210633 vp1839 cassette is expressed from a VSV105 plasmid.
records.label: VP1839 system

records.description: The element Sn, distinct from organotin compounds, dissolved inorganic tin, tin minerals, indium tin oxide and tin-bearing waste resources. The United States 2025 list's Tin designation is mapped to this element; it does not automatically designate tributyltin or contaminated sediment as critical. The curated microbial experiment concerns organotin ligand transformation, not destruction of the tin element or production of metallic tin.
records.label: Tin

records.description: A tight ring-shaped septin-based cytoskeletal structure that forms at the cell cortex in the division plane, including the bud-neck septin ring of budding yeast and related fungal septin rings at septation sites.
records.label: septin ring

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a two-component Dodola locus represented by DolA and DolB profiles that can protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection.
records.label: Dodola system

records.description: The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding the mating projection.
records.label: mating projection membrane

records.description: The central portion of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body, which spans the periplasm and threads through the rings.
records.label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, rod

records.description: The thick, loosely cross-linked peptidoglycan layer between the spore core and the coat of a mature bacterial endospore.
records.label: endospore cortex

records.description: Sm-like — a Pfam clan (CL0986); a superfamily grouping of evolutionarily related Pfam families sharing structure/function.
records.label: Sm-like

records.description: A physiological enzyme-activity phenotype in which a cell exhibits gamma-glutamyltransferase/glutathione-hydrolase activity, processing glutathione, glutathione-S-conjugates, or other N-terminal L-gamma-glutamyl substrates through a gamma-glutamyl-enzyme intermediate.
records.label: gamma-glutamyltransferase activity

records.description: Either of the lipid bilayers that surround a chloroplast and form the chloroplast envelope.
records.label: chloroplast membrane

records.description: A biochemical test that detects urease enzyme activity by observing urea hydrolysis (typically via a pH-indicator color change). The test outcome (positive or negative) is captured by its child classes; this class itself does not assert urease activity.
records.label: urease test

records.description: A chloroplast inner-envelope protein translocon complex that forms the inner-membrane step of nuclear-encoded preprotein import into the chloroplast.
records.label: Tic complex

records.description: Hybrid — a Pfam clan (CL0105); a superfamily grouping of evolutionarily related Pfam families sharing structure/function.
records.label: Hybrid

records.description: A nutritional phenotype in which a fungus consumes nematodes as food.
records.label: fungal nematophagy

records.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of pyruvate, 2-oxopropanoate.
records.label: pyruvate catabolic process

records.description: The central axis/core of the ear (distal end of the lateral branch/ear shoot) upon which the kernels (caryopses) are borne. The cob is similar to the central spike of the tassel (male inflorescence) in that it produces multiple rows of paired spikelets (polystichous phyllotaxy).
records.label: cob

records.description: A chromosome that encodes the nuclear genome and is found in the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell during the cell cycle phases when the nucleus is intact.
records.label: nuclear chromosome

records.description: A structure composed of peptidoglycan and often chitin in addition to other materials. It usually forms perpendicular to the long axis of a cell or hypha and grows centripetally from the cell wall to the center of the cell and often functions in the compartmentalization of a cell into two daughter cells. An intercellular cross-wall layer composed of peptidoglycan in dividing bacteria, pseudomurein/S-layer in archaea, or chitin and beta-glucan in yeasts and filamentous fungi that forms perpendicular to the longitudinal cell axis to partition daughter cells or hyphal compartments. Synthesis of the cell septum is directed by the cytokinetic FtsZ divisome in prokaryotes or the actomyosin contractile ring and septin collar in fungi.
records.label: cell septum

records.description: A small, threadlike secretory organelle that forms part of the apical complex and lies close to the subpellicular microtubules.
records.label: mononeme

records.description: A trophic type in which an organism uses molecular hydrogen as an electron donor for energy generation and carbon dioxide as the primary carbon source.
records.label: hydrogenotrophic

records.description: An essential outer kinetochore complex involved in the attachment of microtubule ends to the chromosomes during mitosis.
records.label: Ndc80 complex

records.description: An intranuclear inclusion at the nucleolar periphery in which nuclear factors collect reversibly during acute heat stress or starvation.
records.label: nucleolar peripheral inclusion body

records.description: A large lattice-like axial structure found in some flagellated protists which extends alongside the axoneme. Protein components of the paraflagellar rod are likely implicated, among other, in adenine nucleotide signaling and metabolism, and in calcium signaling.
records.label: paraflagellar rod

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses the two-gene DefensePredictor-discovered system 28 locus cataloged as working transcriptional unit ANEX and whose plasmid expression in E. coli MG1655 reduced bacteriophage plaquing.
records.label: DS-28 system

records.description: Any of the long, generally straight, hollow tubes of internal diameter 12-15 nm and external diameter 24 nm found in a wide variety of eukaryotic cells; each consists (usually) of 13 protofilaments of polymeric tubulin, staggered in such a manner that the tubulin monomers are arranged in a helical pattern on the microtubular surface, and with the alpha/beta axes of the tubulin subunits parallel to the long axis of the tubule; exist in equilibrium with pool of tubulin monomers and can be rapidly assembled or disassembled in response to physiological stimuli; concerned with force generation, e.g. in the spindle.
records.label: microtubule

definition_sources: NCBIfam PGAP (composed from product and EC/GO annotations)
records.description: checkpoint protein rad24 — a functionally conserved protein family grouped by the NCBIfam full-length profile-HMM TIGR00602 (subfamily).
records.label: checkpoint protein rad24

records.description: A type of endosome in which regions of the limiting endosomal membrane invaginate to form internal vesicles; membrane proteins that enter the internal vesicles are sequestered from the cytoplasm.
records.label: multivesicular body

records.description: Nuclear bodies frequently found near or associated with Cajal bodies (also called coiled bodies or CBs). Gemini of coiled bodies, or 'gems', are similar in size and shape to CBs, and often indistinguishable under the microscope. Unlike CBs, gems do not contain small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs); they contain a protein called survivor of motor neurons (SMN) whose function relates to snRNP biogenesis. Gems are believed to assist CBs in snRNP biogenesis, and to play a role in the etiology of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).
records.label: Gemini of Cajal bodies

records.description: The smaller of the two subunits of a ribosome.
records.label: small ribosomal subunit

records.description: Translocases — EC 7.-.-.-, an Enzyme Commission classification node.
records.label: Translocases

records.description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lactate, the anion of lactic acid.
records.label: lactate biosynthetic process

records.description: A fungal mating phenotype in which compatibility between partners is governed by a single segregating mating-type factor.
records.label: bipolar mating system

records.description: Protection mechanism used by plants and cyanobacteria under conditions of excess energy absorption as a consequence of the light reactions of photosynthesis.
records.label: photoprotection

records.description: signal recognition particle receptor FtsY. FtsY, the bacterial signal-recognition particle (SRP) receptor (SR), is homologous to the SRP receptor alpha-subunit (SRalpha) of the eukaryotic SR. It interacts with the signal-recognition particle (SRP) and is required for the co-translational membrane targeting of proteins
records.label: FtsY

records.description: A constriction site at the junction of the plasma, flagellar and flagellar pocket membranes where the flagellum emerges from the cell body. Observed in some unicellular eukaryotic species such as Chlamydomonas, Giardia and Trypanosoma.
records.label: ciliary pocket collar

records.description: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's inability of being turned, bowed, or twisted without breaking.
records.label: inflexible

records.description: Cell recognition involving the deposition of specific pathways in the extracellular matrix that guide migrating cells.
records.label: contact guidance

records.description: A spliceosomal complex that is formed following the second splicing event and contains the spliced product, the excised intron, and three snRNPs, including U5.
records.label: post-spliceosomal complex

records.description: A cytoskeletal structure in some kinetoplastid species linking the structures of the ciliary pocket collar and the flagellum attachment zone (aka cilium attachment zone).
records.label: bilobe structure

records.description: A membrane-bounded organelle that receives incoming material from primary endocytic vesicles that have been generated by clathrin-dependent and clathrin-independent endocytosis; vesicles fuse with the early endosome to deliver cargo for sorting into recycling or degradation pathways.
records.label: early endosome

records.description: The volume enclosed by the magnetosome membrane.
records.label: magnetosome lumen

records.description: The formation of spores derived from the products of meiosis.
records.label: sexual sporulation

records.description: A mitotic cell cycle checkpoint that delays mitotic sister chromatid separation and consequently the mitotic metaphase/anaphase transition until the spindle is correctly assembled and chromosomes are attached to the spindle. Spindle assembly checkpoint signaling begins with the activated Mph family kinase, and results in the inhibition of the Anaphase Promoting Complex and its activator Sleepy/Cdc20 by the mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC).
records.label: mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint signaling

records.description: A colony morphology characterized by the overall macroscopic colony outline as observed on solid medium.
records.label: colony shape

records.description: Patricin A is a streptogramin B antibiotic.
records.label: patricin A

records.description: Protein complex forming the elongated portion of the radial spoke between the base which binds to the A-tubule of each microtubule outer doublet and the neck which connects to the spoke head within the ciliary or flagellum axoneme.
records.label: radial spoke stalk

records.description: A multimeric protein complex that associates with the vacuolar membrane, late endosomal (multivesicular body) and lysosomal membranes. HOPS is a tethering complex involved in vesicle fusion.
records.label: HOPS complex

records.description: SCOPe dm-level node 'Actinin' (sccs i.15.1.1).
records.label: Actinin

records.description: The region of a kinetochore most external to centromeric DNA; this outer region mediates kinetochore-microtubule interactions.
records.label: outer kinetochore

records.description: A solubility quality inhering in a substance by virtue of the bearer's disposition to dissolve in a liquid.
records.label: soluble in

records.description: The process in which tubulin alpha-beta heterodimers begin aggregation to form an oligomeric tubulin structure (a microtubule seed). Microtubule nucleation is the initiating step in the formation of a microtubule in the absence of any existing microtubules ('de novo' microtubule formation).
records.label: microtubule nucleation

records.description: A biological macromolecule (typically a protein, occasionally a catalytic RNA) that catalyses a specific biochemical reaction. This class is the material-entity sense of "enzyme" (the molecule itself), matching METPO:1000527's placement as a subclass of METPO:1000186 (material entity). Used as the range class for METPO enzyme-related OBJECT_PROPERTYs (shows_activity_of, enzyme_activity_analyzed, does_not_show_activity_of).
records.label: enzyme

records.description: A protein complex involved in septin ring formation during mitosis. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae it consists of BNI5, CDC3, CDC10, CDC11, CDC12, GIN4, NAP1 and SHS1. At least 2 GIN4 molecules are involved.
records.label: Gin4 complex

records.description: The creation of a single nucleus from multiple nuclei as a result of fusing the lipid bilayers that surround each nuclei.
records.label: karyogamy

records.description: A bacterial cytoplasmic-membrane Sec-pathway protein-conducting channel built from SecY, SecE, and SecG, through which unfolded secretory proteins or nascent membrane proteins move during translocation or membrane insertion.
records.label: SecYEG translocon complex

records.description: A physiological phenotype in which a non-genetic cellular state established by prior carbon-source conditions persists after those conditions change and alters subsequent induction or growth responses to carbon sources.
records.label: carbon-source memory

records.description: A cell surface furrow that wraps around a dinoflagellate cell; the transverse flagellum lies in it.
records.label: dinoflagellate cingulum

records.description: A natural depression or hole in the surface topography caused by the removal of soil or bedrock, often both, by water. Sinkholes may vary in size from less than a meter to several hundred meters both in diameter and depth, and vary in form from soil-lined bowls to bedrock-edged chasms.
records.label: sinkhole

records.description: A COPI membrane vesicle coat complex found associated with Golgi membranes; it forms on COPI-coated vesicles that mediate Golgi-to-endoplasmic-reticulum retrograde transport.
records.label: COPI vesicle coat

records.description: A Y-shaped protein complex in the ciliary transition zone that connects the cilium axoneme to the ciliary necklace. Both protein sorting and protein gating occur at this point in the cilium allowing some, but not all proteins to enter the cilium.
records.label: Y-shaped link

records.description: A membrane-bounded vesicle found predominantly in Plasmodium female gametocytes, that becomes progressively more abundant as the gametocyte reaches full maturity. These vesicles lie beneath the subpellicular membrane of the gametocyte, and the release of their contents into the parasitophorous vacuole has been postulated to aid in the escape of gametocytes from the erythrocyte after ingestion by the mosquito.
records.label: osmiophilic body

records.description: A nuclear body that is found in the germinal vesicles of amphibian oocytes, and consist of three major parts: a remarkably spherical body about 5-10 pm in diameter, smaller spherical or nearly spherical granules on the surface, and inclusions of various sizes that strongly resemble the surface granules. The parts of the sphere organelle have distinct compositions, including splicing snRNAs and proteins.
records.label: sphere organelle

records.description: An intracellular membrane-bounded particle found in fungi and containing chitin synthase; it synthesizes chitin microfibrils. Chitin synthase activity exists in chitosomes and they are proposed to act as a reservoir for regulated transport of chitin synthase enzymes to the division septum.
records.label: chitosome

records.description: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's passing into solution.
records.label: dissolved

records.description: Organized structure of distinctive morphology and function, bounded by a single or double lipid bilayer membrane. Includes the nucleus, mitochondria, plastids, vacuoles, and vesicles. Excludes the plasma membrane.
records.label: membrane-bounded organelle

records.description: Cation transporters — a SEED/BV-BRC subsystem subclass; a curated classification grouping of prokaryotic functional modules (subsystems).
records.label: Cation transporters

records.description: A histone deacetylase complex which deacetylates histones preferentially in promoter regions. Composed of a two copies of catalytic histone deacetylase subunit (S. pombe Clr6/ S. cerevisiae Rpd3p), an Sds-3 family protein (S. pombe /S. cerevisiae Sds3(p) ), two copies of SIN3 family co-repressor (S. pombe Pst1/ S. cerevisiae Sin3p, a WD repeat protein/ histone chaperone (S. pombe Prw1/ S. cerevisiae Ume1p), and a zf- PHD finger ( S. pombe Png2/ S. cerevisiae Pho23p), plus 4 additional subunits, and associated factors.
records.label: Rpd3L complex

records.description: Enzymatic activity — sulfhydrogenase (EC 1.12.98.4). Catalysed reaction: n sulfur + H2 = (n-1) sulfur + hydrogen sulfide + H(+).
records.label: sulfhydrogenase

records.description: A diffuse ring composed of a series of septin bars that run parallel to the long axis of the cell. This type of septin structure has been observed in a number of locations associated with polarized growth and/or deposition of new membrane, but not with cytokinesis, such as at the shmoo (mating projection) neck, at the junction between the mother cell and the germ tube (hypha) of a fungal cell growing filamentously.
records.label: septin band

records.description: A histone deacetylase complex that is part of the chromatin remodeling machinery. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae this complex contains Snt2p, Ecm5p and Rpd3p.
records.label: Snt2C complex

records.description: A histone deacetylase complex that is involved in transcriptional regulation. In S. cerevisiae, this complex consists of Set3p, Snt1p, Hos4p, Sif2p, Cpr1p, Hos2p, and Hst1p.
records.label: Set3 complex

records.description: An extracellular electrically conductive Geobacter sulfurreducens PCA filament assembled as a helical array of OmcS six-heme c-type cytochrome monomers whose stacked hemes provide a path for long-range electron transport.
records.label: OmcS cytochrome nanowire

records.description: Catalysis of the release of the N-terminal pyroglutamyl group from a peptide or protein.
records.label: pyroglutamyl-peptidase activity

records.description: A plasmid-encoded bacterial tubulin-like cytoskeletal filament assembled from TubZ GTPase subunits that supports pBtoxis plasmid partitioning in Bacillus thuringiensis.
records.label: TubZ filament

records.description: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments that make up the cis-Golgi network.
records.label: cis-Golgi network membrane

records.description: A jumbo-bacteriophage protein-shelled compartment that assembles in infected bacterial cells, surrounds replicating phage DNA, and spatially separates phage genome replication and transcription from bacterial translation.
records.label: phage nucleus

definition_sources: InterPro:IPR045110 abstract (PANTHER PTHR12609 is a member signature)
records.description: XMAP215 proteins, such as Alp14 and XMAP215 (also known as CKAP5), increase microtubules dynamic polymerization rates by recruiting soluble alpha/beta-tubulin via their conserved TOG domains to polymerizing microtubule plus ends. The TOG domain contains HEAT repeats, forming a oblong paddle-like structure. CKAP5 plays a major role in organizing spindle poles and acts as component of the TACC3/ch-TOG/clathrin complex proposed to contribute to stabilization of kinetochore fibres of the mitotic spindle by acting as inter-microtubule bridge. Proteins in this family also includes the XMAP215 homologue, Stu2 from budding yeasts and Alp14/Dis1 from fission yeasts.
records.label: MICROTUBULE ASSOCIATED PROTEIN XMAP215

records.description: A spliceosomal complex that is formed by association of the 5' splice site and the branch point sequence with specific snRNPs. The prespliceosome includes many proteins in addition to those found in the bound snRNPs. Commitment to a given pair of 5' and 3' splice sites occurs at the time of prespliceosome formation. Prespliceosome complexes are not active for splicing, but are instead an early step in the assembly of a spliceosomal complex.
records.label: prespliceosome

records.description: A pyrimidotriazine that is 1,6-dimethyl-1,5,6,7-tetrahydropyrimido[5,4-e][1,2,4]triazine with oxo groups at positions 5 and 7.
records.label: toxoflavin

records.description: Enzymatic activity — peptidylglycine monooxygenase (EC 1.14.17.3). Catalysed reaction: a [peptide]-C-terminal glycine + 2 L-ascorbate + O2 = a [peptide]-C- terminal (2S)-2-hydroxyglycine + 2 monodehydro-L-ascorbate radical + H2O.
records.label: peptidylglycine monooxygenase

records.description: The long, thin external propeller of the bacterial-type flagellum, formed by polymerized flagellin.
records.label: bacterial-type flagellum filament

records.description: The outer, i.e. cytoplasm-facing, lipid bilayer of the plastid envelope.
records.label: plastid outer membrane

records.description: A phenotype in which germ-tube emergence or hyphal extension is directionally biased away from neighboring cells or hyphae of the same species.
records.label: negative autotropism

records.description: Patricin B is a streptogramin B antibiotic.
records.label: patricin B

records.description: A ribosome contained within a chloroplast.
records.label: chloroplast ribosome

records.description: The outermost layer of the spore wall, as described in Saccharomyces.
records.label: dityrosine layer of spore wall

records.description: A symbiosis in which the microorganism benefits from the association (e.g. resources, shelter, transport) while the host's fitness remains essentially unaffected.
records.label: commensalism

records.description: A multiprotein kinetochore subcomplex that binds to centromeric chromatin and forms part of the outer kinetochore. It helps to recruit outer kinetochore subunits that will bind to microtubules. In humans, it consists of MIS12, DSN1, NSL1 and PMF1.
records.label: MIS12/MIND type complex

records.description: A marine hydrothermal vent chimney which is built of brucite and calcium and magnesium carbonates precipitated where low-temperature, hyperalkaline, hydrogen- and methane-rich fluid produced by serpentinization of ultramafic rock mixes with seawater.
records.label: serpentinization-hosted carbonate hydrothermal vent chimney

records.description: A pathogen that infects organisms in the kingdom Viridiplantae.
records.label: plant pathogen

records.description: The portion of the microtubule cytoskeleton that lies just beneath the plasma membrane.
records.label: cortical microtubule cytoskeleton

records.description: AVAST type 1 anti-phage system protein Avs1c — a functionally conserved protein family grouped by the NCBIfam full-length profile-HMM NF041811 (equivalog).
records.label: AVAST type 1 anti-phage system protein Avs1c

records.description: The lipid bilayer surrounding an esterosome. This membrane has characteristics of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) membranes.
records.label: esterosome membrane

records.description: Respiratory chain complex IV is a membrane-bound cytochrome c oxidase complex that transfers electrons from reduced cytochrome c to dioxygen and couples oxygen reduction to proton translocation across a respiratory membrane.
records.label: respiratory chain complex IV

records.description: An anaerobic respiration in which an organism uses fumarate as the terminal electron acceptor and reduces it to succinate for energy conservation.
records.label: fumarate respiration

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses the two-gene DefensePredictor-discovered system 12 locus cataloged as working transcriptional unit PD3A and whose plasmid expression in E. coli MG1655 reduced bacteriophage plaquing.
records.label: DS-12 system

records.description: Arrays of septin filaments, or bars, found in a series of filamentous structures; observed in the prospore membrane during spore formation.
records.label: prospore septin filament array

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses the two-gene HEC-03 Hma-embedded candidate locus, encoding an ABC ATPase and an associated PilT N-terminal domain protein, that can reduce bacteriophage plaquing.
records.label: HEC-03 system

records.description: A membrane coat found on coated pits and some coated vesicles; consists of polymerized clathrin triskelions, each comprising three clathrin heavy chains and three clathrin light chains, linked to the membrane via one of the AP adaptor complexes.
records.label: clathrin coat

records.description: Responsible for the transport of xenobiotics, such as drugs, out of the cell, in particular from the periplasm. Single-component efflux transporters remove toxic compounds from the cytoplasm to the periplasmic space where tolC-dependent transporters expel them from the cell. Transports acriflavines and indoles. Member of the Resistance-Nodulation-Division (RND) family of efflux pumps. Expression of this system is generally low but it appears to be up-regulated when expression of AcrAB-TolC (CPX-4263) is impaired or in the presence of specific classes of xenobiotic. A curated stable macromolecular complex (Complex Portal) with 3 subunits.
records.label: AcrEF-TolC multidrug efflux transport complex

records.description: metallopeptidase — an OrthoDB orthologous group at the Bacteria level.
records.label: metallopeptidase

records.description: Cinnabar is the trigonal mercury sulfide mineral alpha-HgS, distinct from cubic metacinnabar, hypercinnabar, elemental mercury and unspecified Hg-S particles. The September 2026 IMA list gives grandfathered status but an unknown original-description year; no approval accession is inferred. The curated study concerns laboratory mercury mobilization from source-assigned commercial cinnabar, not microbial formation of the species or isolation of a recovered product. No criticality designation is inherited from mercury or sulfur.
records.label: Cinnabar

records.description: A colony shape that has a branching, root-like outline.
records.label: rhizoid colony

records.description: Extracellular amyloid fibers assembled from CsgA by the Csg secretion and nucleation machinery that form a pilus subtype in enteric biofilm matrices.
records.label: curli

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a Brigantia locus represented by a VCA0419 profile that can protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection.
records.label: Brigantia system

records.description: A membrane-bounded vesicle inside a multivesicular body that forms when the limiting endosomal membrane buds inward and pinches into the lumen during multivesicular body sorting.
records.label: multivesicular body intraluminal vesicle

records.description: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a Bil bacterial ubiquitin-like conjugation locus that can covalently attach a ubiquitin-like protein to the bacteriophage central tail fibre and impair phage infectivity.
records.label: Bil system

records.description: Magnetite is the Fe(II)Fe(III)2O4 mineral species, grandfathered in the September 2026 IMA list with original-description year 1845. It is distinct from elemental iron, maghemite, ferrihydrite and a mixed magnetic precipitate. The experiment below forms a magnetite-rich, probably cation-deficient mixed product from synthetic ferrihydrite; it does not demonstrate pure ideal magnetite or recovery from natural magnetite ore. The Ax17 assay is also represented under iron and the paired ferrihydrite/magnetite record; these are substrate/product perspectives on one experiment, not independent replication. No iron criticality designation is inherited.
records.label: Magnetite

records.description: The dense, protein-rich outermost layer of a microsporidian spore wall that lies above the endospore.
records.label: microsporidian-type exospore

records.description: Complex that transfers electrons from reduced plastoquinone to oxidized plastocyanin and translocates protons from the stroma to the lumen. The complex contains a core structure of three catalytic subunits: cytochrome b, the Rieske iron sulfur protein (ISP), and cytochrome f, which are arranged in an integral membrane-bound dimeric complex; additional subunits are present, and vary among different species.
records.label: cytochrome b6f complex

records.description: DISARM system phospholipase D-like protein DrmC — a functionally conserved protein family grouped by the NCBIfam full-length profile-HMM NF038319 (equivalog).
records.label: DISARM system phospholipase D-like protein DrmC

records.description: A physiological enzyme-activity phenotype in which a cell produces active caseinase proteases that hydrolyze casein.
records.label: caseinase activity

records.description: Any of the thin, flattened membrane-bounded compartments that form the central portion of the Golgi complex.
records.label: Golgi cisterna

records.description: A part of the respiratory chain, containing the 13 polypeptide subunits of cytochrome c oxidase, including cytochrome a and cytochrome a3. Catalyzes the oxidation of reduced cytochrome c by dioxygen (O2).
records.label: respiratory chain complex IV

records.description: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell actively reduces the end-to-end extension of its stalk.

records.description: This entry represents Activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID), which is a single-stranded DNA-specific cytidine deaminase. It is involved in somatic hypermutation, gene conversion, and class-switch recombination in B-lymphocytes by deaminating C to U during transcription of Ig-variable and Ig-switch region DNA. It is required for several crucial steps of B-cell terminal differentiation necessary for efficient antibody responses. The AID/APOBEC are deaminases that function in RNA/DNA editing. The AID/APOBEC family contains several subfamilies: AID, APOBEC1, APOBEC2, APOBEC3, APOBEC4 and APOBEC5. AID/APOBEC deaminases (AADs) convert cytidine to uridine in single-stranded nucleic acids. They are involved in numerous mutagenic processes, including those underpinning vertebrate innate and adaptive immunity. APOBEC were suggested to originate from ancestral AID genes expressed in the lymphocytes of jawless fish over 500 million years ago. Gene duplication and diversification of AID structure and function, probably contributed to the evolutionary process leading to genes that encode the APOBEC proteins of amphibians, birds, and tetrapods including primates.
records.label: Activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID)

records.description: XMAP215/Dis1 proteins, such as Alp14 and XMAP215, increase microtubules dynamic polymerization rates by recruiting soluble alpha/beta-tubulin via their conserved TOG domains to polymerizing microtubule plus ends. This entry represents a structural domain with an armadillo (ARM)-like fold, consisting of a multi-helical fold comprised of two curved layers of α- helices arranged in a regular right-handed superhelix, where the repeats that make up this structure are arranged about a common axis. These superhelical structures present an extensive solvent-accessible surface that is well suited to binding large substrates such as proteins and nucleic acids. Domains and repeats with an ARM-like fold have been found in a number of proteins, including: ARM repeat domain, found in beta-catenins, importins, karyopherin and exportins. HEAT repeat domain, found in protein phosphatase 2a and initiation factor eIF4G. PHAT domain, found in the RNA-binding protein Smaug. Leucine-rich repeat variant, which contain an FeS cluster. Pumilio repeat domain, found in Pumilio protein. Regulatory subunit H of V-type ATPases. PBS lyase HEAT-like repeat. Mo25 protein. MIF4G domain-like, found in eukaryotic initiation factor eIF4G, translation initiation factor eIF-2b epsilon and nuclear cap-binding protein CBP80. The N-terminal domain of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit 12. The C-terminal domain of leukotriene A4 hydrolase. The helical domain of phosphoinositide 3-kinase. The N-terminal fragment of adaptin alpha-C and beta subunits. The proximal leg segment and the linker domain of the clathrin heavy chain. The sequence similarity among these different repeats or domains is low, however they exhibit considerable structural similarity. Furthermo…
records.label: TOG domain

records.description: This entry represents the HAT repeat in Pre-mRNA-splicing factor SYF1, CLF1 and related proteins that bind RNA from eukaryotes and prokaryotes. The HAT (Half A TPR) repeat has a repetitive pattern characterised by three aromatic residues with a conserved spacing. They are structurally and sequentially similar to TPRs (tetratricopeptide repeats), though they lack the highly conserved alanine and glycine residues found in TPRs. The number of HAT repeats found in different proteins varies between 9 and 12. HAT-repeat-containing proteins appear to be components of macromolecular complexes that are required for RNA processing. The HAT motif has striking structural similarities to HEAT repeats (InterPro:IPR000357), being of a similar length and consisting of two short helices connected by a loop domain, as in HEAT repeats. Some studies have suggested that the HAT repeats may be involved in protein-protein interactions. However, the HAT repeats of Arabidopsis HCF107 protein have been shown to bind RNA.

records.description: LOTUS is an uncharacterized small globular domain found in Limkain b1, Oskar and Tudor-containing proteins 5 and 7. LOTUS is an uncharacterized small globular domain found in Limkain b1, Oskar and Tudor-containing proteins 5 and 7. The LOTUS containing proteins are germline-specific and are found in the nuage/polar granules of germ cells. Tudor-containing protein 5 and 7 belong to the evolutionary conserved Tudor domain-containing protein (TDRD) family involved in germ cell development. In mice, TDRD5 and TDRD7 are components of the intermitochondrial cements (IMCs) and the chromatoid bodies (CBs), which are cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein granules involved in RNA processing for spermatogenesis. Oskar protein is a critical component of the pole plasm in the Drosophila oocyte, which is required for germ cell formation. Limkain b1 is a novel human autoantigen, localized to a subset of ABCD3 and PXF marked peroxisomes. Limkain b1 may be a relatively common target of human autoantibodies reactive to cytoplasmic vesicle-like structures. Limkain b1 contains multiple copies of LOTUS domains and a conserved RNA recognition motif. The exact molecular function of LOTUS domain remains to be characterized. Its occurrence in proteins associated with RNA metabolism suggests that it might be involved in RNA binding function. The presence of several basic residues and RNA fold recognition motifs support this hypothesis. The RNA binding function might be the first step of regulating mRNA translation or localization
records.label: LOTUS

Some evidence suggests that DNA polymerase epsilon is the leading strand polymerase; it is also involved in nucleotide-excision repair and mismatch repair.

records.description: A complex that tethers COPII vesicles at ER-Golgi intermediate compartment. Its role in this part of the vesicular transport may start at the ER exit sites. Binds to a component of the COPII coat. In yeast it includes the following subunits: Bet3 (as homodimer), Bet5, Trs20, Trs23, Trs31, Trs33 which are regarded as the core subunits of all TRAPP complexes in yeast.
records.label: TRAPPI protein complex

records.description: An ISWI complex that contains an ATPase subunit of the ISWI family (SNF2H in mammals, Isw2 in S. cerevisiae), an ACF1 homolog, and additional small histone fold subunits (generally two of these, but Xenopus has only one and some additional non-conserved subunits). records.description: Invagination of the plasma membrane from which a cilium (also called flagellum) protrudes.

records.description: A physiological enzyme-activity phenotype in which a cell produces active valine arylamidase enzymes that hydrolyze valine arylamide substrates.
records.label: valine arylamidase activity

records.description: The outer, i.e. cytoplasm-facing, lipid bilayer of the nuclear envelope; continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum of the cell and sometimes studded with ribosomes.

records.description: Disco-interacting protein 2 (Dip2). However, its function may have diverged from other members of the superfamily. In mouse embryo, Dip2 homolog A plays an important role in the development of both vertebrate and invertebrate nervous systems. Dip2A appears to regulate cell growth and the arrangement of cells in organs. Biochemically, Dip2A functions as a receptor of FSTL1, an extracellular glycoprotein, and may play a role as a cardiovascular protective agent
records.label: Dip2

records.description: Anti-CRISPR type I subtype F4. AcrIF4 is a phage anti-CRISPR (Acr) protein that has been shown to associate with the type I-F Cascade surveillance complex (type I-F Csy complex) to inhibit DNA binding. AcrIF4 binds the Csy complex with affinities that are orders of magnitude weaker than Acr proteins like AcrIF1 and AcrIF2. The type I-F Csy complex is a crRNA-guided surveillance complex composed of a crRNA and nine Cas proteins (one Cas8f, one Cas5f, one Cas6f, and six Cas7f), which recruits a nuclease-helicase protein Cas3 for target degradation. CRISPR-Cas immune systems are used by certain prokaryotes and archaea to resist the invasion of foreign nucleic acids such as phages or plasmids. Anti-CRISPRs are small proteins which are the natural inhibitors for CRISPR-Cas systems; encoded on bacterial and archaeal viruses, they allow the virus to evade host CRISPR-Cas systems. The CRISPR-Cas-mediated adaptive immune response can be divided into three steps, including the acquisition of spacer derived from invading nucleic acids, crRNA processing, and target degradation. Theoretically, Acr proteins could suppress any step to disrupt the CRISPR-Cas system. Acr proteins are diverse with no common sequence or structural motif, which inhibit a wide range of CRISPR-Cas systems using various inhibition mechanisms. Weak and strong Acr-phages often cooperate to overcome CRISPR resistance, with a first phage blocking the host CRISPR-Cas immune system to allow a second Acr-phage to successfully replicate which leads to epidemiological tipping points. CRISPR-Cas systems are divided into two classes (1 and 2) and six types (class 1: types I, III and IV; class 2: types II, V and VI). Class 1 systems utilize RNA-guided complexes consisting of multiple Cas proteins as the effector proteins to recognize and cleave target DNA. Type I CRISPR-Cas systems are the most widespread in nature, and the Cas protein composition of the employed CRISPR ribonucleoprotein (crRNP) complexes differs between seven subtypes (A to F, U). Acr families are named for their type and subtype which are numbered sequentially as they are discovered
records.label: AcrIF4
